readerMoment: Has scoped an owned network, identified its router and subnet, and made a read-only listener list for one owned host. The router shows an unfamiliar list of device names and addresses.
outcome: Can produce a dated, private baseline of their owned devices and known listeners, compare a later snapshot, and investigate a changed or unknown entry before acting.
coreModel: A baseline is a dated comparison point, not a verdict: router observations and host observations are incomplete, so a difference becomes a question to verify.

teachingShape.realTask: Make a dated private device and listener inventory without scanning or changing anything
activate: Bring the owned-host listener list from the previous page
Open the router's connected devices or client list for an authorized network
demonstrate: Join two invented device observations to a host listener record
Compare snapshots showing one changed address and one genuinely unresolved device
apply: Record each owned device, where it was observed, identity evidence, and confidence
Record known listeners on hosts the reader owns; mark devices without local access as unchecked
integrate: Date and store the baseline privately; compare after a deliberate change or on a chosen cadence

requiredIdeas: Router client and DHCP lists may be partial or stale; a device can be offline, on guest Wi-Fi, or absent from that router view.
A name, local IP or MAC address is a clue, not proof of ownership; addresses can change and private/randomized MACs complicate matching.
The baseline contains device identity and role, observed address, where and when seen, owner/authorization, listener details on owned hosts, and unknowns.
Compare before/after by corroborated device identity, not just IP; distinguish expected changes from unresolved ones.
An unknown entry calls for verification with an owner or device, not disconnection, probing or public posting.
visualNeeds: A compact before/after comparison showing an address change for a known device versus a new unresolved device

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Active port scans or touching other people's devices
deliberatelyExcluded.why: This page joins read-only router and owned-host observations.
A name or address alone cannot prove an intruder; response needs separate verification.
Those changes belong to later lessons.

nextPagePressure: A baseline can now support cautious decisions about exposure and network boundaries.
candidateAnalogies: A dated household inventory: absence from one room does not mean an item is gone; check another location before changing the list.
